_info: Stock (standard) configuration of ONE engine, loaded automatically when this engine is selected and by the button 'Load stock configuration'. File name = engine id. 'chargers': a catalog id (string) or {"profile": {...}, "count": n} for a part that belongs to this engine only. Maps use the shared rpm axis [800,2000,3500,5000,6000,7000] and load axis [0,25,50,75,100] ([loadIdx][rpmIdx]). 'reference' holds a known factory power figure for later calibration.
name: VW EA827 2.0L 8v - stock configuration
generated: ignition and fuel maps derived from the shared base maps: rpm axis stretched to this engine's redline, fuel scaled by displacement per cylinder, ignition for a naturally aspirated engine (low-load row, 0.1 deg retard per % load)

reference.standard: PS as published by kfz-tech.de (German manufacturer data), converted to mechanical hp with 1 hp = 1.01387 PS
reference.source: kfz-tech.de VW Golf 2.0 (1994-1997): 85 kW (115 PS) at 5400 rpm, 166 N·m at 3200 rpm, 10:1, 82.5 x 92.8 mm; fastcarcheck.uk Golf 2.0 (EA827, 1991-2000): 115 hp, 166 N·m at 3200 rpm, 5400 rpm
reference.notes: Bore/stroke 82.5 x 92.8 mm and compression 10.0:1 match the file. A regional Brazilian catalogue listing (57.5 hp/L, about 114 cv, 16.7 kgfm) agrees with this power figure. Wikipedia's EA827 table lists a 2.0 8V with 10.0:1 and 90 PS at 5500 rpm (codes ABS/ADZ/ANP), a different and lower-output spec, so it is not used. A fastcarcheck.uk entry lists 10.4:1 for the same displacement, which is also not used.
